answer_in_one_paragraph: AI-written (Fable), 16 November 2026. Neither link holds as a theorem. (1) Apart, both ways. `ConfinedRise.ends` is a lineage ending with a whole whose conditions fall below their gate and do not return, the excess anyone's. `line_ends` is a line ending alone, below its own need, on a stock that can recover while other units go on (C). The Web-with-a-Flow dictionary is an obstacle here too (the statement needs a flow and a web defined from the course), but it is not why they are apart: C balances at every step. What decides whether the line takes the whole with it is the order of needs: where the line has one need and every other unit needs at least that, the net ends when the line does (argued by hand, one side only; 1,500 random worlds, none against). (2) The ending laws are not cases of each other. The rise is one definition: `generations_rise` is `MoreThanNow` unfolded, so `need_unmet` does derive the step-by-step rise, from `grows`, which stays supplied. It is not derived from what taking gains: a unit's kids do not depend on its use.

links.statement: A closed line whose kids of the line take more is a `ConfinedRise` on the stock, its excess derived.
links.evidence: Founding.lean:161-175; LineOnAStock.lean:904-911. Under `ends`' base premises, with one condition whose level is the course's: `excess` and balance make the level fall throughout [T, T+n); afterwards `family_excess_ends` (Continuation.lean:573) with `gated` and `acting` leaves nothing given; `draws` puts T at or before the line's last step. So the level never rises from T on. In C it does.
links.first_obstacle: The whole does not end; `grows` is of take, `Rise.selected` of offspring number (B).

links.statement: A confined rise gives a line whose kids take more.
links.evidence: `Body.confined_rise` (Founding.lean:741): the confined founder takes one at step 0, its offspring nothing; `kids` differs by step (:438). `take`, `give` and `kids` are free in time: no rule.

links.statement: `lineage (generations need kids giving use (w, x)) h k = []` under `line_ends`' premises, for a line whose kids are all of it.
links.evidence: It restates `line_ends` in `SelectionLevels.lineage` and stays true if `ConfinedRise` changes; both sides already share `SelectionTerm.Generations` (LineOnAStock.lean:560, :664). Why nothing returns differs: there the gate keeps the conditions down; here the level may return and `closed` leaves no unit to restart.

links.statement: One is a case of the other by a definition unfolded.
links.evidence: Exhaustion.lean:117 takes `Balances`, at most `B` given a step, and a take that is a ledger entry. TurningInTime.lean:669 takes a cap on the level, `FromNothing`, and a use that is a draw asked, cut off at the level. After the counting the arguments differ.

links.statement: `more_accumulates` (Exhaustion.lean:51): `(∀ i, i < n → MoreThanNow id g (T + i)) → g T + n ≤ g (T + n)`. `TurningInTime.rises_from` (:625) is its case T = 0, proved again by induction.
links.standing: already a theorem that shows it, of the counting only; condition 4 does not apply (no path)
links.evidence: `MoreThanNow q g n := q (g n) < q (g (n + 1))` (Seeking.lean:73). By the same unfolding `generations_rise` (LineOnAStock.lean:985) and `rising_takes_all`'s `rises` are `MoreThanNow`: a renaming. By reading.
links.imports_it_would_add: None if `more_accumulates` moves to Seeking, which both already import; Exhaustion is not in TurningInTime's closure.

A take not covered or growing: `excess`, `start`, the uptake anyone's (`draws` unused) | `grows`, with `keeps`, `high` | `more`, with `keeps`, `high`. Nothing of the level reaching how it selects: absent | by construction, with `down` | `outside`, `un`. Needing what it uses up: `confined`, `gated` | `needs` | `needs`.

against_the_four_conditions: `rises_from` from `more_accumulates`: (1) both sides' definitions, no structure: met. (2) no premise added: met. (3) false if `MoreThanNow` were `≤`: met. (4) no path. It joins a lemma beneath both dynamics, not the two atlas entries.
Nothing else is called a theorem: the line as a confined rise fails (1) and is false on C.
